body:
# the contributor audit of the double-core support triangle and corner compression

Source: `candidate fd39a28eeb41e9c4`.

not compatible mixed-fiber replacement theorems.

Exact core-sector area forces equality of the entire closed convex sector
with its core triangle. Any point of the body beyond the bridge line
would, by joining it to an interior bridge point, create positive sector
area beyond that triangle. Hence all three bridge lines really support
the same body, giving its containment in the three displayed halfplanes.
The cap identities imply X_i>Y_i under the strict half-cap ceiling.

An unbounded intersection has a nonzero recession vector by normalization
of an escaping sequence. Each bridge functional is strictly positive
on its own closed double cone, so no such vector lies in a double cone
or on a source ray. Relabeling its unique cone gives exactly
alpha<=u/s<=1-beta, with alpha,beta positive and alpha+beta<=1.

I checked both neighboring-sector envelopes in their actual ray
coordinates. In sector 2, m>0, m<=1, n>=-1, and 1+mn>0 give the stated
quadrant polygon and area even at a collapsed auxiliary vertex. In
sector 3, w>0, s<=1, w<=1, and 1-sw>0 give the second polygon and area;
s is allowed to be negative. The third support inequality is only
discarded for an upper bound. Both determinants and simplified area
formulas agree with direct substitution.

Multiplying the two strict area requirements by the positive factors
2beta D_2 and 2alpha D_3 gives the claimed coefficients -ell on B^2
and -1 on b^2. Dividing by a and completing the two squares yields
exactly

  (B-beta*t)^2/t+(b-alpha*a)^2/a
       +(1-alpha-beta)(beta*t+alpha*a)<0.

This contradicts nonnegativity and proves boundedness. Three distinct
halfplanes with a strictly interior origin then give a triangle. Each
ray is already blocked at its prescribed endpoint by an actual bridge
line, so the triangle has exactly the same six ray endpoints.

For the separate finite compression, the inner six-ray hull and the
other two triangle vertices fill everything except the one indicated
corner triangle. A parallel homothetic cut with ratio sqrt(E/L) removes
exactly the missing area, stays in that unique corner, and retains all
six ray endpoints. Its sector, cap, total-area and chord data therefore
agree exactly with the original body. E=0 gives the triangle; 0<E<=L
gives an actual quadrilateral, including the full-corner cut.

In the (2S,2S,2D) application, alternating positive double sectors are
excluded by multiplying X_i>Y_i and comparing the equal products of
the unique and double core areas. In the other orientation all double
sectors are cores. Positive excess in every unique sector puts the
support triangle vertices strictly in those sectors. The two singular
blocks force the reconstructed corner vertices onto both actual bridge
lines; hence their sector areas are the full triangle sector areas.
Containment and equal convex-sector area then put those vertices in the
original body itself. This avoids assuming that arbitrary reconstruction
vertices belong to the original body. The finite compression therefore
applies and preserves every selected generalized row exactly.

The other pentagon graph types and the row inequality on the remaining
quadrilaterals remain separate obligations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
